statement:
Problem Statement
There are
N
mochi (rice cakes) arranged in ascending order of size.
The size of the
i
-th mochi
(1 \leq i \leq N)
is
A_i
.
Given two mochi
A
and
B
, with sizes
a
and
b
respectively, you can make one kagamimochi (a stacked rice cake) by placing mochi
A
on top of mochi
B
if and only if
a
is at most half of
b
.
You choose two mochi out of the
N
mochi, and place one on top of the other to form one kagamimochi.
Find how many different kinds of kagamimochi can be made.
Two kagamimochi are distinguished if at least one of the mochi is different, even if the sizes of the mochi are the same.
Constraints
2 \leq N \leq 5 \times 10^5
1 \leq A_i \leq 10^9 \ (1 \leq i \leq N)
A_i \leq A_{i+1} \ (1 \leq i < N)
All input values are integers.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N
A_1
A_2
\cdots
A_N
Output
Print the number of different kinds of kagamimochi that can be made.
Sample Input 1
6
2 3 4 4 7 10
Sample Output 1
8
The sizes of the given mochi are as follows:
In this case, you can make the following eight kinds of kagamimochi:
Note that there are two kinds of kagamimochi where a mochi of size
4
is topped by a mochi of size
2
, and two kinds where a mochi of size
10
is topped by a mochi of size
4
.
Sample Input 2
3
387 388 389
Sample Output 2
0
It is possible that you cannot make any kagamimochi.
Sample Input 3
32
1 2 4 5 8 10 12 16 19 25 33 40 50 64 87 101 149 175 202 211 278 314 355 405 412 420 442 481 512 582 600 641
Sample Output 3
388

constraints_guess.notes: The input size N is between 2 and 5e+05, and the size of each mochi A_i is between 1 and 10^9.

complexity.why: The algorithm uses a two-pointer technique with a single loop through the array of mochi sizes.

bottlenecks.detail: The current algorithm only counts the number of pairs of mochi that can be stacked, but it does not consider the case where two mochi of the same size can be stacked in different orders.

plans.name: Two-Pointer Technique with Binary Search
plans.core_idea: Use two pointers to iterate through the array of mochi sizes and apply binary search to find the valid pairs.
steps: Sort the array of mochi sizes in ascending order.
Initialize two pointers, one at the beginning and one at the end of the array.
Iterate through the array and for each mochi, use binary search to find the largest mochi that can be placed on top of it.
Count the number of valid pairs and update the result.

plans.name: Improved Two-Pointer Technique
plans.core_idea: Use an improved two-pointer technique to iterate through the array of mochi sizes and count the valid pairs.
steps: Initialize two pointers, one at the beginning of the array.
Iterate through the array and for each mochi, move the second pointer to the largest mochi that can be placed on top of it.
Count the number of valid pairs and update the result.

plans.name: Algebraic Optimization
plans.core_idea: Use algebraic optimization to simplify the counting of valid pairs.
steps: Use a single loop to iterate through the array of mochi sizes.
For each mochi, calculate the maximum size of the mochi that can be placed on top of it.
Count the number of valid pairs and update the result.

plans.name: Optimize Input and Loop
plans.core_idea: Preserve the algorithm while optimizing input handling and loop structure
steps: Use ios::sync_with_stdio(false) and cin.tie(nullptr) to optimize I/O
Replace generic loops with a single-case path where applicable
Eliminate per-iteration temporary containers and tiny allocations

plans.name: Improve Data Locality and Reduce Rescans
plans.core_idea: Enhance data locality and reduce unnecessary rescans
steps: Profile the dominant work and count row touches, column touches, rescans, branches, memory writes, and state rebuilds
Separate construction, transition, validation, and answer reconstruction
Maintain persistent buckets or queues keyed by the current label/state

plans.name: Apply Hot Path Specialization and State Compression
plans.core_idea: Apply hot path specialization and state compression for optimization
steps: Recover complete paired sources and locate the first semantic divergence
Hoist invariant calculations out of inner loops and cache repeated values
Prefer contiguous vector or array storage and replace map/set with sort plus scan

plans.name: Invariant Driven Single Pass Compression
plans.core_idea: Replace simulation-heavy, state-sprawling, or multi-pass C++ solutions with the smallest representation implied by the invariant.
steps: Identify the dependency: adjacent state, monotone frontier, frequency counts, positional mapping, parity class, or order-sensitive simulation.
Remove any intermediate array whose entries are consumed exactly once; accumulate directly in the producer pass.
Fold uniform initialization and global adjustments into one baseline.
For adjacent recurrences, retain only previous/current scalars and stream the input.
For monotone greedy constraints, maintain the smallest sufficient frontier and update it immediately; never revisit finalized positions.

plans.name: Frequency First Aggregation and Domain Compression
plans.core_idea: Reusable optimization pattern distilled from weighted traces.
steps: Determine whether the result depends on order, or only on the multiset of values and their frequencies.
Choose the representation: flat frequency array for a safe dense bounded domain, coordinate-compressed vector for sparse values, or a hash/map for online sparse updates.
Accumulate counts while reading whenever later logic needs only frequencies; avoid storing and reordering the full input unless reconstruction requires positions.

plans.name: Compress Small State Dynamic Programs
plans.core_idea: When a C++ solution uses a large or repeatedly materialized DP for a process with a tiny finite state space, expose the true state invariant, remove redundant dimensions, and optimize the implementation around adjacent-layer transitions.
steps: State the invariant precisely: define what each DP state represents and identify which parts of history affect future transitions.
Construct the minimal sufficient state. Collapse equivalent digit identities, endpoint pairs, carry histories, or ordering classes into a small mode or automaton state.
Remove dimensions that are only used by adjacent layers. Replace full tables with two contiguous rows, one rolling buffer, or a few scalar variables.
